distractors.reason: 'Look for' means search for something you have not found yet. We don't use it to mean observe a picture that is already in front of you.
'Look after' means take care of someone or something. It does not describe viewing a picture.
'Look into' means investigate a problem or a question. It is not used for simply viewing pictures.

example_sentence: Please ___ the pictures in this comic strip.
l1_interference: Türkçe'de 'bakmak' fiili edat almadan doğrudan nesne alabilir, bu yüzden Türkçe konuşanlar 'look the picture' der. Oysa İngilizcede doğrusu 'look at the picture'dır; 'at' edatını unutmamak gerekir.
explanation: In English, 'look' needs the preposition 'at' to show that you direct your eyes toward something. The verb and preposition work together as one unit.

related_collocations.example: Listen to the story on the radio.
We wait for the next comic strip every Sunday.
Children often believe in the hero of the story.

memory_tip: LOOK + AT = turn your eyes toward something you can see now | LOOK FOR = search | LOOK AFTER = care for
